keep: The idea is named in one line up front (vectors add nose to tail, and the resultant is the arrow from the first tail to the last nose), with the resultant's quote on exactly the words it supports.

The picture is the brief's forces on a ring: pulls dragged on the ring, the same arrows laid nose to tail beside it, the resultant as the gap, a needle working by parts, and the equilibrant as a dashed arrow that closes the chain and drops the needle to zero. The brief names that cause and effect.

One worked example computed from the rule: A = 4i + 1j and B = 1i + 3j kN give 5i + 4j, 6.40 kN, against 7.28 kN for the sizes added. The misconception is shown failing with real numbers, and again with two 3 kN pulls at 0°, 90°, 120° and 180°.

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (11, 12). Each lesson 3 mistake in the brief has a puzzle with its own wrong pick: sizes added (2, 12), Pythagoras on arrows not at right angles (11), 'the forces cancel' (10), nose to tail against the parallelogram and the sum never drawn (5, 6), equilibrant signs (8).
Four footnotes, one per sentence, each on a rule he might look up. No source is named in the text.
fix: Causal step skipped: '3 kN at 120°' is stated without a reason. Say the chain's corner is then 60°, so its triangle has three equal sides.
Causal step skipped: 'to hold the ring still, the pulls must add to nothing' has no reason. Say that any gap left over is a net pull, and a net pull sets the ring moving.
Causal step skipped: the parallelogram is asserted. Say why B first reaches the same nose: the across parts and the up parts add to the same sums in either order.
Common mistake 'joining the noses ... is not the sum' says only what is wrong. Say what is right: the sum is the diagonal from the shared tail.
ignores: 'which the turning effect of a force deals with' is vague. Name it plainly: the turning effect is a moment, and it needs another kind of product.
The analogy's 'its total change of place is nothing' is stiff. Say the chain ends where it began, so its legs add to nothing.
No false absolutes found: 'sizes add only when the pulls point the same way' holds at every angle (equal only at 0°), and 'opposite ropes cancel only along their own line' is true.
